```yaml
name: Stale Issue and Pull Request Handler

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 0 * * *' # Runs at midnight UTC every day
  issues:
    types: [opened, edited]
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, edited]

jobs:
  stale-issue-handler:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v2

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v2
        with:
          node-version: '14'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install

      - name: Run stale issue handler script
        run: npx @actions/stale --repo-token ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} --days-before-stale 90 --days-before-close 180 --label "stale"

  stale-pr-handler:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v2

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v2
        with:
          node-version: '14'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install

      - name: Run stale PR handler script
        run: npx @actions/stale --repo-token ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} --days-before-stale 90 --days-before-close 180 --label "stale"
```

This GitHub Actions workflow file `.github/workflows/stale.yaml` sets up two jobs:

1. **Stale Issue Handler**: This job runs daily at midnight UTC to mark issues as stale if they haven't been updated in over 90 days and close them after 180 days. It uses the `@actions/stale` tool to manage the staleness of issues.

2. **Stale PR Handler**: Similar to the issue handler, this job marks pull requests as stale if they haven't been updated in over 90 days and closes them after 180 days. It also uses the `@actions/stale` tool for managing the staleness of pull requests.

The workflow ensures that both issues and pull requests are regularly checked and managed for staleness, helping to keep the repository clean and focused on active contributions.
